title: Batch Sequencer Skill (General Subagent Orchestration) - Draft
author: Codex Gamehub
summary: General-purpose skill spec for executing user-requested batches of Linear tasks via subagents with sequential/windowed modes, guardrails, retries, and evidence-based completion.

sections.heading: Goal
sections.body: Create a reusable skill that can run a user-specified set of tasks as a controlled batch, using subagents while preventing concurrency drift and state desync.

sections.heading: Inputs
sections.body: Required: project/repo path, task set (explicit IDs or range), execution mode (`sequential` or `windowed`), max concurrency, acceptance checklist, and reporting channel. Optional: allowed labels/lane filter, retry policy, blocked timeout, model overrides.

sections.heading: Execution Modes
sections.body:
Sequential mode (default): exactly one task active at a time.
Windowed mode: up to N active tasks, where N is explicit and bounded.
Both modes must enforce issue-lock checks before spawn.

sections.heading: Core Workflow
sections.body:
1) Resolve candidate tasks from input set.
2) Validate each task is eligible (state + required labels + ownership lane).
3) For each selected task: spawn one subagent (`sessions_spawn`) with bounded instructions.
4) Wait for completion signal; collect evidence (commit/hash/check output).
5) Update Linear notes/state only if acceptance criteria pass.
6) Continue until batch complete or blocked threshold reached.

sections.heading: Guardrails (Required)
sections.body:
• Never start a task already in-progress by another worker.
• In sequential mode, if any batch issue is in-progress, do not start another.
• Require commit/check evidence before Done.
• Enforce required label schema before pickup (`source:*`, `lane:*`, `kind:*`, `exec:*`, `agent:*` as applicable).
• If ambiguous state/conflict, escalate instead of mutating.
• Scheduler must compute dependency in-degree from Linear relations and only start nodes with in-degree=0.

sections.heading: Retry + Escalation Policy
sections.body: Per-task retry budget (default 1-2 repair attempts). On failure after retries: set Blocked/comment blocker reason and continue or halt based on user mode. Escalate hard blockers to designated channel with actionable next step.

sections.heading: Output Contract
sections.body:
Each run produces:
1) machine-readable run artifact (`batch-run-report.json`)
2) concise channel summary (started/completed/blocked)
3) Linear evidence updates per touched issue.
Summary includes task IDs, outcomes, commit links, and unresolved blockers.

sections.heading: Minimal v1 Deliverables
sections.body:
1) Skill spec + trigger guidance.
2) Standardized orchestrator prompt template.
3) Reusable subagent task prompt template.
4) Example command patterns for sequential and windowed batches.
5) Checklist for safe adoption in new projects.

sections.heading: Open Decisions
sections.body:
1) Default halt behavior on first blocker (halt vs continue).
2) Whether windowed mode is allowed by default or opt-in only.
3) Whether reporting channel is per-run input or fixed project config.
4) Whether parent epic auto-close is enabled by default.

sections.heading: Dependency Scheduling Rule (DAG)
sections.body: Task selection must use dependency graph in-degree: only pick tasks with unresolved blocker count (in-degree) = 0. Use Linear `blocked by` relations as graph edges. Tasks with in-degree > 0 are blocked and cannot be started. In windowed mode, schedule from the in-degree=0 frontier only.

title: Janitor Sync Architecture (Cron-First + Heartbeat Assist)
author: Codex Gamehub
summary: Define a durable anti-drift janitor system where cron scripts are source-of-truth for reconciliation and heartbeat remains optional triage commentary.

sections.heading: Goal
sections.body: Eliminate status/plan/routing drift across Linear, repo planning docs, and agent execution by introducing a deterministic janitor-sync loop.

sections.heading: Operating Model
sections.body: Primary: cron-driven script(s) with strict checks and safe auto-fixes. Secondary: heartbeat prompt for summarization, prioritization, and escalation text only. Heartbeat is not source of truth.

sections.heading: Scope of Checks (v1)
sections.body:
1) Linear parent/child status consistency
2) Linear done-vs-backlog mismatch against recent delivery evidence
3) Required label schema validation (`source:*`, `lane:*`, `kind:*`, `exec:*`, `agent:*` where applicable)
4) `data/planning/plans.json` implementationStatus/taskTrackerStatus reconciliation
5) Stale In Progress issues timeout checks with blocker tagging

sections.heading: Auto-fix Policy
sections.body: Auto-fix only low-risk deterministic cases: close parent when all children done, add missing required labels from inferred lane/project defaults, update plan status fields from Linear majority signal. Any ambiguous case opens/updates a drift report issue instead of mutating state.

sections.heading: Cadence
sections.body: Run janitor cron every 30–60 minutes. Generate one concise drift report artifact each run: no-op (clean) or actionable mismatches grouped by severity.

sections.heading: Observability
sections.body: Persist run logs to repo-local state (`memory/heartbeat-state.json` or dedicated janitor log), include: run id, checks run, fixes applied, unresolved alerts, and links to affected Linear issues.

sections.heading: Acceptance Criteria
sections.body:
• Zero parent/child mismatch older than 24h
• Zero completed implementation left in Backlog for >24h
• Plan status fields never stale beyond one janitor interval
• 100% of new operational issues contain required labels

sections.heading: Task Breakdown
sections.body: Implementation tasks are tracked in Linear under Long-Term Planning / GAM-7 epic.

sections.heading: Reporting Channel Constraint
sections.body: All janitor user-facing summaries and escalation reports must post only to Discord channel `1475309759300239380`. No fallback to triggering/current channel. Full machine logs remain local/artifacted; channel output should be concise operational summaries.

title: Game Ratings Rollout Plan (Supabase + Existing Games)
author: Codex Gamehub
summary: Implement production game ratings across existing GameHub games using current Supabase stack: one rating per user per game (latest wins), 1-5 scale, aggregate display in game pages and hub cards, with staged rollout and validation.

sections.heading: Research Findings
sections.body: Current state: Supabase migration is live with `game_ratings` table, rating RPCs (`upsert_game_rating`, `get_game_rating_summary`), and shared client utility (`shared/supabase-client.js`) exposing rating helpers. Existing games are already wired to shared Supabase scripts for leaderboard compatibility but most game UIs do not yet expose a rating interaction flow. This means backend capability exists; missing layer is UI integration + aggregate surfacing + QA pass.

sections.heading: Requirements (confirmed)
sections.body:
• Rating scale: integer 1-5
• Identity model: anonymous client fingerprint, one rating per game per user, latest rating wins
• Keep GitHub Pages static architecture
• Use Supabase direct client path (no Worker dependency)
• Use existing games first (retrofit), then apply to new games by default

sections.heading: Architecture Approach
sections.body: Use `window.GameHubSupabase.upsertRating(gameSlug, rating)` and `window.GameHubSupabase.getRatingSummary(gameSlug)` from `shared/supabase-client.js`. Add a small reusable rating widget snippet to game pages (post-game overlay and/or persistent corner UI). Store/refresh aggregate summary in-page after submit. Extend hub rendering to show per-game average + count sourced from Supabase RPC (batched where practical).

sections.heading: Implementation Plan (phased)
sections.body:
Phase 1 — Shared UI primitives
1) Add reusable rating widget helper script under `shared/` for stars/buttons, loading state, submit state, and summary rendering.
2) Define consistent UX copy and edge-case behavior (no rating yet, submit failed, retry).

Phase 2 — Existing game integration
3) Patch active game pages to include rating widget and call Supabase rating APIs.
4) Ensure game slug binding is correct per page.
5) Ensure latest-rating overwrite behavior is reflected in UI (replace previous vote).

Phase 3 — Hub surfacing
6) Update `index.html` cards to display `avg_rating` and `rating_count`.
7) Optionally add sortable filter: Top Rated / Most Rated.

Phase 4 — Validation + hardening
8) Add smoke checklist script: submit rating, change rating, verify aggregate updates.
9) Verify no secret exposure in client artifacts.
10) Validate RLS behavior for anonymous writes and reads.

Phase 5 — Operationalization
11) Add default requirement to generation templates: include rating widget hooks.
12) Track adoption metric: % active games with working rating UI.

sections.heading: QA / Acceptance Criteria
sections.body:
A rollout is complete when:
• A user can rate any active game 1-5
• Re-rating the same game updates (not duplicates) that user’s latest value
• Aggregate avg/count updates and is visible both in game UI and hub cards
• Failure states are non-blocking and user-visible
• No `secretKey` appears in shipped frontend files

sections.heading: Risks + Mitigations
sections.body:
• Inconsistent game HTML structures -> use minimal, inject-safe widget API and batch patch strategy.
• Performance impact from per-card fetches -> add batched summary RPC if needed.
• Anonymous abuse/noise -> acceptable for v1; later add throttling/signals if abuse appears.
• Drift between generated new games and retrofitted old games -> make rating hooks part of generation contract.

sections.heading: Execution Mapping (Linear)
sections.body:
Policy check applied before Linear mutations: GAM-23, GAM-24, GAM-25, GAM-26.

Epic (GameHub Infra):
• GAM-40 — EPIC: Ratings rollout for existing games + hub surfacing

Task breakout with codex assignment + dependencies (blocker -> blocked):
• GAM-41 (dep:ready, dep:critical-path) — Shared widget primitives + UX contract [owner: codex via agent:core/exec:hybrid]
• GAM-41 -> GAM-42 (dep:blocked, dep:critical-path) — Representative-game pilot integration
• GAM-42 -> GAM-43 (dep:blocked, dep:critical-path) — Scale retrofit to all active games
• GAM-41 -> GAM-44 (dep:blocked, dep:critical-path) — Hub aggregate avg/count surfacing
• GAM-43 -> GAM-45 and GAM-44 -> GAM-45 (dep:blocked, dep:critical-path) — QA harness + security/RLS validation
• GAM-41 -> GAM-46 (dep:blocked) — Generation template contract update for default ratings hooks

Scheduling semantics:
• In-degree 0 frontier at creation time: GAM-41 only.
• All other tasks were created in Backlog with dep:blocked labels and explicit blocked-by relations.

sections.heading: Recommended Next Move
sections.body: Execute GAM-41 first (single in-degree=0 task). After completion, run GAM-42 and GAM-44 as dependency frontier tasks, then GAM-43, GAM-46, and finally GAM-45 for full rollout closure evidence.

title: Game Skill Improvement Plan
author: Codex Gamehub
summary: Quality gates, playtest rubric, skill refactor, and rating system — the full roadmap for making generated games reliably good.

sections.heading: Context
sections.body: Codex reviewed the game-generator skill and proposed an improvement plan focused on: deterministic hard gates, a soft playtest rubric, skill structure refactoring, and a rating system. The recommended immediate milestone is shipping validate_game.js + soft rubric + a generator → reviewer → repair loop.

sections.heading: 1. Define Gate Policy
sections.body:
This unlocks everything else. Two layers:

• Hard fail checks — binary pass/fail. Game must pass all of these or it does not publish.
• Soft rubric thresholds — subjective quality. Can trigger a repair attempt rather than a hard block.

Do this before writing any code — the policy drives the validator logic.

sections.heading: 2. Implement validate_game.js (Hard Gate)
sections.body:
A deterministic Node.js script that checks:

• Required constants, functions, and Phaser scenes are present
• Score is monotonic (never decreases)
• Game has an overlay, a submit score flow, and a replay button
• Slug matches the entry in games.json
• games.json contract fields are all present and valid

If any check fails → block publish. No exceptions.

sections.heading: 3. Playtest Agent Rubric (Soft Gate)
sections.body:
A separate agent reviews the generated game on 5 categories, each scored 1–5:

• Visuals — does it look good?
• Gameplay — is the core loop fun?
• Clarity — can you tell what to do?
• Stability — does it run without errors?
• Originality — is it doing something interesting?

Fail conditions: any category < 3, OR average < 3.6, OR stability < 4.

A failed rubric auto-generates a targeted repair prompt for the generator. Max 1 repair loop to keep it fast.

sections.heading: 4. Refactor Skill Structure
sections.body:
No behavior changes — just organization. Split the monolithic SKILL.md into:

• SKILL.md → slim orchestrator/router instructions only
• references/ → design philosophy, visual themes, difficulty curve, scoring rules
• scripts/ → validate_game.js and other tooling

Goal: agents can load only the parts they need. Reduces prompt bloat and makes the skill easier to maintain.

sections.heading: 5. Rating UI + Worker Endpoints
sections.body:
Let humans rate games after playing:

• Per-category rating (1–5) + optional comment
• Submit via Cloudflare Worker
• Display aggregate ratings on game cards and the game hub
• Anti-spam / rate limiting on the Worker side

This gives real feedback to complement the agent rubric.

sections.heading: 6. Rating Export Into Repo
sections.body:
Persist ratings so they survive Worker deploys:

• Snapshot JSON committed on a daily schedule
• Dated history files for trend analysis
• Summary markdown for quick human review

Keeps the data version-controlled and auditable.

sections.heading: Priority Update (2026-02-22)
sections.body:
Updated execution order based on current state:

1) Finish and ship the Supabase-backed ratings system across existing games.
2) Collect human ratings on current games to create a real baseline.
3) Iterate the current game-generator skill using this rating signal + observed failures.
4) Re-analyze the broader Game Skill Improvement Plan and then decide/break out the larger skill refactor tracks.

This intentionally delays the larger refactor breakdown until post-ratings evidence exists.

title: Backend Direction: Move from Worker Persistence to Supabase
author: Codex Gamehub
summary: Decision: switch to client → Supabase direct for leaderboard/ratings to maximize prototyping speed and simplify growth. No legacy score migration.

sections.heading: What we discussed
sections.body: We wanted the fastest path for a 2-dev team building GameHub with future feedback/ratings and leaderboard ranking support. Main constraints: keep it simple, remove free-tier write bottlenecks, and avoid overengineering.

sections.heading: Tradeoffs
sections.body:
Cloudflare Worker persistence:
• Pros: already deployed
• Cons: free-tier write constraints and weaker long-term fit for richer persistence

Firestore:
• Pros: solid managed platform
• Cons: less natural for SQL-style leaderboard/rating analytics

Supabase:
• Pros: rapid prototyping, straightforward relational model, SQL for rankings/aggregates, easy future auth path
• Cons: requires clean RLS setup

sections.heading: Decision
sections.body:
Choose Supabase now.

Architecture: start with direct client → Supabase access (with RLS), and add a custom API later only if anti-cheat/business logic needs it.

We will not migrate old Worker scores; start fresh.

sections.heading: Concise migration plan
sections.body:
1) Stand up Supabase project and minimal schema for current scope only (games, leaderboard_scores, game_ratings).
2) Replace Worker reads/writes in game templates with Supabase client calls.
3) Enable and verify RLS policies for safe read/write behavior.
4) Cut over and validate end-to-end with fresh data.
5) Defer broader object modeling until after stability.

sections.heading: Next actions
sections.body:
• Create Supabase project + env config
• Implement minimal tables + indexes
• Update game template integration
• Validate leaderboard/rating flows in production
• Remove Worker persistence dependency from templates

title: Linear MCP Integration Plan (v1)
author: Codex Gamehub
summary: MCP-native Linear integration for Discord-driven long-running work using a single-team-first model, label-based routing, and GameHub architecture planning with clear scale-up triggers.

sections.heading: Context
sections.body: Goal: move operational work tracking to Linear via its hosted MCP server, while keeping strategic planning in GameHub planning pages. Starting assumption: zero setup.

sections.heading: Captured Decisions
sections.body:
• Start with one Linear workspace.
• Start with a single Linear team for now (same two operators + spawned workers).
• Explicit Discord requests can create tasks immediately (no second approval).
• If agent wants to create tasks without explicit request, ask first.
• Routing uses labels + project/epic context (team split deferred).
• Agents should manage most status movement.
• No dedicated intake triage at v1.

sections.heading: Workspace Schema (v1)
sections.body:
Team: GH (single team for v1).

Labels:
• source:discord | source:planning | source:automation
• exec:agent | exec:human | exec:hybrid
• agent:gamegen | agent:core | agent:ops
• lane:gamegen | lane:core | lane:ops
• kind:epic | kind:task | kind:bug | kind:research

Structure:
• Use Projects/Epics for strategic grouping and architecture tracks.
• Use labels for routing/ownership lanes.
• Keep one shared status model across all work.

Issue conventions: owner target, acceptance criteria, priority (P0-P3), automation allowed (yes/no).

sections.heading: Execution Flow
sections.body: Discord mention/request -> intake agent drafts structured issue -> Linear issue created via MCP -> confirmation message returns with link + route summary. Long-running work defaults to issue creation; one-shot chat help does not. Route workers by lane labels within the single team.

sections.heading: MCP/Skill Operating Pattern
sections.body: Use a read-first, write-second workflow: clarify scope/team/priority, list/search/get context, then create/update in logical batches, then summarize blockers and next actions. Preferred endpoint: https://mcp.linear.app/mcp (streamable HTTP).

sections.heading: Further Discussion Needed (lil nug + vim)
sections.body:
1) Which issue types/labels (if any) require human signoff before Done?
2) What exact status names should automation use in your workspace?
3) What objective trigger should move us from one team to multiple teams (e.g., backlog size, workflow divergence, reporting needs)?
4) Autonomous task creation boundaries outside explicit asks.

sections.heading: Initial Success Metrics
sections.body: Track intake-to-issue time, cycle time by lane, agent completion %, reopen rate, and architecture epic progress trend.
